What is a liquidation?

A liquidation happens when a leveraged futures position loses so much that its margin can no longer cover the loss, and the exchange force-closes it. A long is liquidated when price falls to its liquidation level; a short when price rises to it. Big clusters of liquidations can cascade and accelerate a move. Work out exactly where your own position would be wiped with the liquidation calculator, see the danger zones on the liquidation heatmap, or practice risk-free in Paper Trade.

Feed aggregates public liquidation streams from multiple exchanges; coverage and timing vary by venue. Educational only, not financial advice.
